source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Totowa NYM2 campus publishes 6 MW of IT capacity and 200,000 square feet of technical space, and nothing about how that power is delivered.

The two numbers describe a building, not a workload. Six megawatts is about 150 racks at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, or about 600 racks at 10 kW. The operator publishes no rack count, no accelerator count, and no power density, so the choice between those readings is the reader's, not the operator's. A campus can hold the same megawatts and be built for either.

The only certification listed is SSAE 16 Type II, which covers controls over financial reporting. It says nothing about electrical topology, cooling method, or on-site generation, and no tenant is named. Suitability for dense AI training cannot be judged from this spec page, and the page does not claim otherwise.

New Jersey has 48 mapped facilities, of which five publish any capacity figure. Those five total 111.3 MW, and this campus contributes 6 MW, about five percent, ranking fourth in the state by published megawatts. Because most of the state's facilities publish no number, 111.3 MW is a floor on New Jersey's data center load, not a measure of it.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
